data.narrative:
Valar Atomics is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Isaiah P. Taylor, currently valued at $6.0B post-money following $1.0B in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public and 8 private—operating in the nuclear energy sector, including Helion (Series F, $15.5B), Oklo (public, $7.0B), and X-Energy (IPO-stage, $5.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $11.4B. Peer-median methodology across three same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables yields $7.0B, with the peer range spanning $5.6B to $15.5B. These methods produced meaningfully different signals, reflecting variance in peer stage maturity and capital-raising trajectory.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $6.0B (low) to $13.1B (high), with a median of $9.2B. The $7.2B spread reflects material uncertainty around appropriate peer selection and stage-adjusted multiples for pre-revenue or early-revenue nuclear ventures. Key drivers of valuation dispersion include heterogeneous commercialization timelines among nuclear peers, regulatory pathway clarity, and whether comparables' valuations reflect genuine market discipline or venture supply-driven premiums.
